raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
-this is a follow-up to #32365. I encountered valid media payloads being rejected in `rust/sglang-mm/src/common/fetch.rs` when they exactly fit the remaining request byte budget. The reader reserved a full chunk before reading and needed another reservation just to check EOF.

-it now reserves up to the available allowance atomically and uses a bounded one-byte EOF probe. A probed byte is charged before appending, including when another reader refunds capacity. It preserves the per-source cap and adds boundary and concurrency regression tests.

## Tests

Passed locally from `rust/` on `fa81606149b6a5206efe3e1a0cda32a3c45f4daa`:

- `cargo test --locked -p sglang-mm`
- `cargo test --locked -p sglang-mm --features parallel`
- `cargo test --locked --workspace`
- `cargo clippy --locked -p sglang-mm --features python,parallel --lib -- -D warnings`
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

-The fetch regressions fail against the unfixed implementation and pass with the fix and targeted refund-race test also fails when the defective probe behavior is restored.

Changed-file pre-commit and `git diff --check` also passed. 
Hosted CI has not run.

## Checklist

- [x] Run pre-commit checks.
- [x] Validate the regression tests and workspace tests.
- [x] Follow existing code style
